title: briza media subsp. elatior
intro: Briza media subsp. elatior, commonly known as quaking grass, is a type of flowering plant that belongs to the Poaceae family. It is native to Europe and Western Asia and is known for its delicate, drooping flowers and grass-like leaves. The plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including inflammation, fever, and respiratory problems, thanks to its health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of Briza media subsp. elatior include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which exhibit therapeutic actions such as analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and spasmolytic effects.
